I1.quote: Searched main text and SI for a measured H2 uptake (gravimetric, volumetric, flow); found none. Every H2 uptake value is computed: "While the theoretical predictions obtained here must be further corroborated by experiment" (main p. 2, Introduction); Table 3 is titled "H2 Uptake and Delivery Obtained from the FH-NLDFT Prediction" (main p. 10). Measured adsorption was Ar 87 K, CO2 273 K, CO2 and CH4 at 313 and 333 K only.

I5.quote: We investigate the effect of heat treatment on the structure of carbide-derived carbons (CDC) prepared by chlorination from nanosized SiC particles and on their methane as well as hydrogen storage and delivery performance.

notes: The abstract's 'improvement in high pressure H2 uptake (4.61 wt % at 77 K)' is an FH-NLDFT prediction: main p. 2 says 'In theory, a H2 uptake of 4.61 wt % at 77 K and 28 bar is obtained', and the Conclusions (p. 13) say 'A theoretical H2 uptake of 4.61 wt % at 77 K and 28 bar'. Figures 8 and 9 are predicted H2 isotherms. The experimental part measures only Ar (87 K), CO2 (273 K; 313 and 333 K to 200 bar), CH4 (313 and 333 K) and He buoyancy (skeletal density). SI Figure S1 compares the model with H2 isotherms 'taken from the literature' (Nguyen et al.; Gogotsi et al.), which are other work's data. The paper is primary research (experimental CH4 and CO2 data), is not marked retracted in record.json or the PDF, and makes no statement that all its data were published before, so not_primary, retracted and duplicate_data do not apply. Text layer checked against the page images of main p. 2 and p. 10.
